findings.claim: note which other consumers (CheckoutFormContainer.tsx, CheckoutPaymentMethodsProvider.tsx) read or depend on that form state
findings.checked: Read src/components/pages/CheckoutPage/CheckoutPaymentMethodsProvider.tsx in full and grepped it for `email`, `confirmEmail`, `useFormContext`, `useWatch`.
findings.found: CheckoutPaymentMethodsProvider.tsx has no reference to email, confirmEmail, useFormContext, useWatch, or ICheckoutFormValues anywhere. It only consumes `cart` (for price/currency) and `useNextLocale()` to configure the Stripe <Elements> provider. It does not read or depend on the email/confirmEmail form state at all. CheckoutFormContainer.tsx, by contrast, does reference `email` at lines 145, 174, 192, 213 — that half of the claim holds.
findings.remedy: Drop CheckoutPaymentMethodsProvider.tsx from the list of consumers of the email/confirmEmail form state, or rephrase to note it only receives cart/locale props and has no coupling to the email fields.

findings.claim: The confirmEmail field's react-hook-form validate rule lives at CheckoutForm.tsx:305-311 and currently does a raw `value !== email` comparison (confirmed by reading the file)
findings.found: The validate function (`if (email && value && value !== email) { return t("TRM774"); }`) spans lines 305-309, not 305-311. Lines 310-311 are the closing `}}` of the rules prop and the start of the unrelated renderLabel prop, not part of the validate rule.
findings.remedy: State the validate rule's line range as CheckoutForm.tsx:305-309.
